For \(a=2015x,\ b=2015y\) with \(\gcd(x,y)=1\), we need
\[
x+y \mid 2015^{2015}\big((x-y)^{2016}+y^{2016}\big).
\]

The previous check showed \(x+y=2,3\) fail. For \(x+y=4\), the coprime pairs \((1,3),(3,1)\) give the bracket odd modulo \(4\), while \(2015^{2015}\equiv 3\pmod 4\), so divisibility by \(4\) fails.

Next, \(x+y=5\). Since \(5\mid 2015\), the factor \(2015^{2015}\) is divisible by \(5\). Thus any coprime pair with \(x+y=5\) works, for example \((x,y)=(1,4)\).

So the minimum is
\[
a+b=2015(x+y)=2015\cdot 5=10075.
\]

\[
\boxed{10075}
\]
